prompt: For a workspace governance check, can you tell me what reactions were left on the message where someone asked about grabbing AWS p5 instance time for the circuit-tracer workload — that message is in the channel where one of our workspace admins sits as a member?
binding_note: r0 (message_reactions) must attach to r1, the specific message asking about p5/supercomputer time for circuit-tracer; r1.channel_id binds to r2, the channel containing it; r3 (channel_members) binds a member of that same r2 to r4 (users); r5 (user_teams) binds that same r4 to a workspace membership carrying the admin/owner role. The admin/owner user need not be the reactor or the message author — only a channel member of r2. No stored message_reactions row satisfies r0 against this r1, so the collection is empty.

obligations.name: reactions_on_supercomputer_message
obligations.description: Reactions (r0) attached to the message (r1) about getting p5 supercomputer time for circuit-tracer, where that message's channel (r2) has a member (r3/r4) holding an admin/owner workspace role (r5). Requested as a collection; the seed contains zero qualifying reaction rows.

task_spec.text: Identify the message about seeking AWS p5 supercomputer time for circuit-tracer in the channel that includes an admin/owner-level workspace member, and report any reactions on it.

access_plan: Locate the message via conversations.history or search.messages on '#engineering' (or workspace-wide search for 'supercomputer'/'p5'), confirm channel membership via conversations.members, cross-check the admin/owner role of that member via users.info or the workspace membership record, then call reactions.get on the identified message's channel/timestamp to enumerate reactions (finding none).
